issues.failure_explanation: The indices $n_T=N\sum_{t\in T}1/p_t$ need not lie in $0\le n<N$: e.g. for $N=30$ and $T=\{2,3,5\}$, $n_T=15+10+6=31\ge N$, so $x_{n_T}$ is out of range for a length-$N$ signal. The stated well-definedness argument only shows the unreduced values are distinct (different lowest-terms denominators); after reducing indices mod $N$, distinctness requires a separate argument (which does hold: if $n_{T_1}\equiv n_{T_2}\pmod N$, multiplying $\sum_{T_1}1/p-\sum_{T_2}1/p\in\mathbb Z$ by the product of the primes in the symmetric difference and reducing mod a prime in $T_1\setminus T_2$ gives a contradiction). The DFT computation in the proof survives once indices are read mod $N$.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof of the following result is identical to \Cref{lem:rep_in_time} and is omitted.

issues.failure_explanation: With the paper's inverse DFT carrying the $1/N$ factor, direct computation gives $y_{dn}=\frac{1}{dN}\sum_{t,k}\tilde x_k e^{\pm 2\pi i(tN+k)dn/(dN)}=\frac1N\sum_k\tilde x_k e^{\pm 2\pi ikn/N}=x_n$, not $dx_n$ (counterexample: $N=1$, $d=2$, $x=[1]$ gives $y=[1,0]$, so $y_0=1\ne 2$). Consistently, Parseval gives $\|y\|^2=\frac1{dN}\|\tilde y\|^2=\|x\|^2$, whereas $y_{dn}=dx_n$ with vanishing off multiples of $d$ would force $\|y\|^2=d^2\|x\|^2$. The duality with lem:rep_in_time fails because the forward transform is unnormalized while the inverse is not, so the omitted 'identical' proof is invalid.

failure_location.quote:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the lemma as $y_{dn}=x_n$ (keeping the vanishing assertion) and account for the $1/N$ normalization in the proof.

issues.title: False scaling constant in the frequency-repetition lemma
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction of the constant fixes the lemma; the only part used downstream (vanishing off multiples of $d$) is correct, so no claim or dependent result is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: From $d_1=\gcd(k,N_1)$ one only gets $\gcd(k/d_1,N_1/d_1)=1$; $\gcd(k/d_1,N_1)$ can exceed 1 (e.g. $N_1=12$, $k=8$: $d_1=4$, $k/d_1=2$, $\gcd(2,12)=2$), so $(k/d_1)^{-1}\bmod N_1$ need not exist and $m_j$ is undefined (also $n_j=h(l/d_2)^{-1}q$ uses an unexplained $h$). The construction only needs the inverse modulo $D_1=N_1/d_1$: the congruence $m_j(k/d_1)\equiv jp\pmod{D_1}$ yields $m_jk\equiv jpd_1\pmod{N_1}$, and the rest of the chain goes through. The lemma's statement is true (the image of $(m,n)\mapsto mkN_2'+nlN_1'\bmod N$ is exactly the multiples of $d$).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: \Require a representative DFT coefficient $\tilde{X}_{k, l}$ for each coefficient class

issues.failure_explanation: For divisors $\lambda>1$ of $D$, the frequency $(\lambda k,\lambda l)$ is in general not the representative of its own class, so $\tilde X_{\lambda k,\lambda l}$ is not among the input coefficients: in $\mathbb Z_4\times\mathbb Z_6$, inverting the $(1,1)$-class needs $\tilde X_{2,2}$ while inverting the $(1,2)$-class needs $\tilde X_{2,4}$, and both frequencies lie in the single class $\{(2,2),(2,4)\}$ whose input supplies only one coefficient (no representative choice can supply both). These values exist only as fill-ins produced by earlier loop iterations, but the ForAll enumeration order is unspecified, so the procedure can call Invert1D with unavailable data.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Specify that RepCoeffs enumerates classes in increasing cyclic-subgroup order (bottom-up), under which each needed $\tilde X_{\lambda k,\lambda l}$ ($\lambda|D$, $\lambda>1$) has already been written by the fill-in of the earlier-processed class of $(\lambda k,\lambda l)$.
issues.overall_effect: alg:2D's stated contract (invert from one representative coefficient per class) is not guaranteed as specified; the later memoized algorithm alg:memo_2D is structured differently and is not affected.
issues.title: High-level 2D inversion algorithm reads coefficients not guaranteed by its input
issues.why_classification: Adding the required enumeration-order specification is a short, local edit that makes the procedure well defined and preserves its guarantee; no result or scope is lost.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Recovering ${\bf x}^{(2)}$, ${\bf x}^{(3)}$, and ${\bf x}^{(6)}$ is trivial, since every DFT coefficient is required to ensure uniqueness of length 2, 3, and 6 signals.
If ${\bf x}$ is a vector of length $N$ consisting of integer entries, then ${\bf x}$ can be uniquely determined by measurements of the $\tau(N)$ DFT coefficients,

issues.failure_explanation: By the paper's own minimal-sampling results, uniqueness requires only $\tau(N)$ coefficients, and $\tau(4)=3<4$ and $\tau(6)=4<6$; unique inversion does not require all coefficients for $N=4$ or $N=6$. The true property of $\{1,2,3,4,6\}$ is $\phi(N)\le 2$, i.e. the algorithm's assembled data (decimated signals plus one coprime coefficient and its conjugate) already covers every frequency, which is why the guess is exact and the subproblems trivial. Both passages conflate $\phi(N)\le 2$ with $\tau(N)=N$ and contradict the paper's own uniqueness theory.

failure_location.quote: For certain values of $N$, including $N = 1, 2, 3, 4, 6$, unique inversion requires all DFT coefficients.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reword both statements to the correct fact: for $N\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$, $\phi(N)\le 2$, so the algorithm's available data comprises all DFT coefficients.
issues.overall_effect: Two passages misstate the sampling requirements for small composite $N$; the algorithmic conclusions they support (trivial subproblems, immediately correct guess) remain correct.
issues.title: False claim that unique inversion requires all DFT coefficients for N in {1,2,3,4,6}
issues.why_classification: A local rewording replaces the false claim with the correct fact; no theorem, algorithm, or guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The basis of eq:lattice_basis has $N+1+\sum_{p\mid N}N/p+2M$ real rows ($N$ identity rows, one $\beta_0$ row, $N/p_j$ rows per prime block of ${\tt B}_1$, and $2M$ real rows for ${\tt B}_2$). For $N=30$, $M=1$ this is $30+1+31+2=64$, not $N+\phi(N)+2M=40$; moreover $\sum_{p\mid N}N/p=N\sum_{p\mid N}1/p$ is not $O(N)$ uniformly (e.g. primorial $N$), so the claimed $O(N^7\log^2 MNL)$ per-iteration bound is not established for the basis as constructed (it omits a $\log\log N$ factor).

failure_location.quote:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the correct ambient dimension $n=N+1+\sum_{p\mid N}N/p+2M=O(N\log\log N)$ (or row-reduce the ${\tt B}_1$ blocks to $N-\phi(N)+1$ rows, giving $n=O(N)$) and restate the bound accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: The stated pseudo-polynomial per-iteration runtime bound for alg:memo_1D/alg:memo_2D rests on a false row count and is not established as written; the algorithms' correctness is unaffected.

issues.why_classification: Correcting the dimension count changes the complexity bound by at most a $\log\log N$ factor (or not at all for a row-reduced basis); the algorithm, guarantees, and advertised scope survive.
